txt: *wheezy breathing*
In the middle, heaving and wheezing: big guy, boot size 46, deep marks. Probably carried the victim over. He alone is 130 kilos; add the man in armour and you could easily exceed 220.
Meanwhile, Fat Angus keeps shooting you furtive glances and mumbling uneasily to himself...
Meanwhile, the fat one keeps shooting you furtive looks while mumbling uneasily to himself...
The room falls quiet. So quiet you can hear Angus wheeze.
The sweaty man turns red and looks first down, then around him, apologetically.
This one -- he's sweating profusely and has difficulty breathing. They've smartly kept him out of the conversation thus far. Definitely the weakest link in the chain.
"Boss..." The big guy in the corner speaks up with a wheeze. "There's another in the kitchen. A blue door. I've been there..."
"Boss..." The big guy in the corner speaks up with a wheeze. "There's another on the roof next to her window. Me and Tibbs saw it when we... were replacing..."
"Boss..." The big guy in the corner speaks up with a wheeze. "There's this strange blue door in the kitchen. I've been there..."
"Don't you give her any more trouble!" the fat guy blurts out. "She's just had some bad luck, that's all."
"Go fuck your mom, Dennis."
"Goddamnit, Dennis. You know I can't help it!" His whiny voice is in deep contrast with his stature.
"Guys, seriously. I've seen this. Stop laughing. Is his face drooping?"
"I didn't say anything."
"I have podagra, asshole!"
"I have slow metabolism, Dennis!"
"I left it home. I can't get it, I'm too fucked..." He grabs his chest. "I'm sorry."
"I will boss." The man reaches in his overalls for a cigarette.
"I wonder where that Sylvie is..."
"It wasn't that, it wasn't..." the fat man says with a wheeze. "We didn't shoot him."
"It wasn't that. It wasn't..." the fat man says with a wheeze. "We didn't hit him, okay?"
"It wasn't that. It wasn't..." the fat man says with a wheeze. "We just couldn't get him down, okay?"
"It's not advanced," the heavy man wheezes. "You're just holed up in a coop all day, writing down what they say. It gets hot as hell in there."
"My dad used to... nevermind."
"No." He looks up, startled, his forehead shiny from sweat. A few coiled locks are peeking out from under his warm woollen hat.
"Says they ain't got shit, boss."
"She said she's... building a..." His voice is very quiet. "A pale emitter."
"That's not even funny, Dennis."
"There's another on the roof next to her window. Me and Tibbs saw it when we... were replacing..."
"We didn't kill him! We didn't even *hang him*, he was dead when..." He takes a breath, wheezing.
"We didn't light him on fire!" You hear the fat man wheeze. He's trying to get up. "No one pissed on him either!"
"We didn't light him on fire!" You hear the fat man wheeze. He's trying to get up.
"We were talkin' about radio equipment. She said she's doing Ulan frequencies and a pale-something. I don't know more."
"Whoaa...."
"Yeah but..." The fat man looks up from the table, oblivious. "They're both girls."
"Yeah." The fat guy in the middle lets out a little chuckle. "You're not even being fucked, Dennis."
